walkthroughs.body_html:
Global Hazards — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Global Hazards brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Global Hazards.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: Constructive waves build sandcastles and destructive waves wash them away.
Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.
Climate change only happens in summer.
A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between constructive and destructive waves?
options: The Brandt Line is the boundary between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
Constructive waves build sandcastles and destructive waves wash them away.
Constructive waves have strong swash and weak backwash, building beaches; destructive waves have weak swash and strong backwash, dragging sediment offshore and eroding cliffs.
Big waves are destructive and small waves are constructive.
